[spoiler=The Ruler of the Six Directions Expands in About Three of Them
-
Historical Expansion]King of Stuipendia Tai Shi Huihuang looked out over his vast realm, thousands of miles of land have been swallowed by his great hordes, in all six directions the Tai dynasty rules and Shi is honoured by millions of subjects. But great men are never satisfied, Tai Shi Huihuang is never satisfied with one crown, or one woman, or one life, Tai Shi Huihuang wants everything. He sought immortality, he heard of men from lands consumed by desert storms that lived forever, and if sand eaters may live forever then surely he, Tai Shi Huihuang, King of Stuipendia, founder of the Tai Dynasty and Master of the Four Celestial Elements may likewise be paged in the history of the Jade Palace as an immortal like the Demigods who serve as the Jade Emperor's chambermaids, though of course he himself is no chambermaid, but an equal to those in the palaces of Heaven. 

His silk robes flow gently in the wind as he stands looking over his great city, the tassels on his imperial mianguan follow suit. He looks over his domain shrouded in darkness, the golden light of the golden disc has yet to rise above the mountains of the Jian. There is much to be done, there is always much to do. Tai Shi Huihuang, well past his middle age and his physical prime presses onward pushing himself down towards the lower floors of the Grand Imperial Palace equal to the Stars of the Firimiant. 

He passes by the thousand and one rooms of his palace, each filled with practicalities and delights of all flavours, from the sweetest of cakes to the sourest of apples. Wings of his palace dedicated to every form of servant and slave available to him, for he is the greatest of Kings. He eventually reaches the courtyard, where he strikes the great Tai bell, cast from pure bronze in his likeness to awaken all within the palace. He turns now from this place of beauty into the cold stone of the banquet hall.

The whole palace stirs aching bones snapping in unison as they arise at their Kings calling. Ministers stir from their slumber lest they face the wrath of his supremeness. They make their way to the great banquet hall of a thousand plates. Servants of the King fashion a great breakfast for him and all those within the palace. Chickens kept just down the road from the palace and grabbed and slaughtered, pigs, cows and lambs are likewise butchered for this opening meal of the day. It is here where the first discussion begins, Tai Shi Huihuang raises a lamb chop,

Respected ministers, dignitaries, concubines, servants, and wife! All turn to look at him, I have lived many years, but, I have much more life to live! I must seek eternity, for I am the great Tai Shi Huihuang, the King of this Eternal Realm,  founder of the Tai Dynasty and Master of the Four Celestial Elements. But there is one thing I am not, an immortal! I am a true son of Heaven! Slave to none, and I will not be a slave to time! Eternal youth will be mine to hold, and all the ministers of the Realm will search into every annal of history until the location of the recipe of the elixir of youth may be found!

All in the hall rose and bowed towards his supremeness showing their devotion to his awesome power and great quest. All the Kings men ate their fill and departed, they would begin to undertake the studying of history and alchemy. 

Imperial Scholar of the Most Noble Sciences and Histories specifically regarding those relating to Immortality and the Locations where one might find it, Xi Xi, undertakes seven nights of sleepless toil. He pours over maps of history, locations where the Kings of old and new have searched for immortality. He marks off the locations where these princes have looked. The great Hanean south is full of rabid dogs and tinpot-generals, thus immortality can not be found there, the Way would not rain that indignity upon the world. Thus it must be to the north, as many Kings pursued north, though of course, none would go as far as his King! 

The Imperial Scholar of the Most Noble Sciences and Histories specifically regarding those relating to Immortality and the Locations where one might find it takes his findings and goes to consult with others among his level of scholarship. The collective commission of these scholars is noted to be known as the Great Imperial Assembly for the Pursuit of Eternal Life for Tai Shi Huihuang, King of Stuipendia, founder of the Tai Dynasty and Master of the Four Celestial Elements. This organisation of the most learned within Stuipendia along with the Imperial Men-at-Arms of the Eternal General and King Tai Shi Huihuang, draws out the great campaign for the search. It carves across a wide berth of the great Tai Shi Huihuang Eternal Imperial Corridor along the Great Sea of the Emptied Bladder of Tai Shi Huihuang, stopping along the River of the Inferior Peoples who refused to speak the same language of his Supremeness, then sweeping across eastward to the islands in the Ocean of the Golden Disc using the Supreme Navy of the Eternal Admiral and King Tai Shi Huihuang. Following their search and conquest the Supreme Navy of the Eternal Admiral and King Tai Shi Huihuang will then return to the Palace, immortal where he will reign until the Jade Emperor gives up his throne and or respects  Tai Shi Huihuangs position as an equal in the court of Heaven.

From their drawing rooms and place of planning, designated rightfully as the Room of Planning for the Expansion of the Six Direction Kingdom,  they would exit and make their way to the Throne Room of Ten Thousand Anunshoto Roses, humbly trotting before and prostrating themselves in front of  Tai Shi Huihuang. They present to his supremeness the map of campaign which he may carry out if he so chooses, no decision is ever made for his supremeness as his all-powerful might would not bow to any mere minister, but despite that he respectfully accepts and graciously permits his generals to explain to him the plan of military action.

General Ju Bu rises, though maintains a slight bend in his posture as he is five foot seven to his supremenesses five foot six and he does not wish to disrespect his King by standing over him, such would be rude and disrespectful to his supremeness as Ju Bu is a mere humble servant in his court which rivals that of the Jade Emperors considering he has a thousand and one rooms whereas the Jade Emperor only has a thousand. 

Ju Bu with his slightly bent posture graciously takes the scroll of the campaign back from Tai Shi Huihuang, and unfurls it, he orders two other servants, both generals in their own right, to rise but not too high and hold on to each edge of the unfurled map. Ju Bu using his hands gestures at the map, now inlaid with gold and jewels from his previous paper form back in the Room of Planning for the Expansion of the Six Direction Kingdom. He begins by pointing at the capital, the seat of Tai Shi Huihuangs eternal kingdom. He metaphorically draws a line along the literal red line in the map inlaid with rubies showing the direction that Tai Shi Huihuang might take if he so wishes, through the Tai Shi Huihuang Eternal Imperial Corridor, along the Great Sea of his Emptied Bladder. Then moving back down south briefly to go through the middle of the Jian mountain area of the  Tai Shi Huihuang Eternal Imperial Corridor. After that, when his army reaches the River of the Inferior Peoples who refused to speak the same language of his Supremeness, Tai Shi Huihuang has the option to use his Imperial Navy to sail across several islands searching them for immortality and of course conquering them in his own name, and then he will return back to his imperial throne room hopefully an immortal.

Tai Shi Huihuang is impressed by the map, and campaign laid forth by his generals, devoted servants to him one and all who would all wilfully lay down their life for him in any instance where it might be required for them to do so. He assents to the plan, though of course, if he had not wished to he would not have, for Tai Shi Huihuang is the King and supreme rule of Stuipendia, thus he can do whatever he wishes in regards to anything at any time he so chooses. But his supreme wiseness and magnanimity allows for him to accept the humble presentation laid forth by his generals and ministers, dictated by Ju Bu.

For three months the Imperial Men-at-Arms of the Eternal General and King Tai Shi Huihuang prepared, by prepare the historians mean, that his supremeness requires the construction of bronze armour inlaid with gold and jewels to match the epic journey he is about to undertake and the forging of such  an imperially supreme set of arms took three months. But when his supremeness dawns his armour at the crack of dawg in Tainuary of the fourteenth year of the rule of Tai dynasty, under the auspices of its founder Tai Shi Huihuang, the great march begins.

It begins of course with a great parade stretching over twenty five kilometres, though that measurement was not used at that time and instead it would have been over four hundred twenty-six thousand seven hundred twenty Tai Shi Huihuangs long or so. The parade of martial might opened with the great imperial army marching on foot, over one hundred and seventy thousand men peacock steeping in perfect order, unwavering in their service. This was followed by a long procession of over nineteen thousand chariots of white horses with manes like silver marching in perfect unison, archers on the literal chariot of the chariots. Armour that shines like the golden disc. Nearing the end of the great column was thirteen elephants resplendent in carpets and castleworks, atop of each was a general and three monkeys to demonstrate his supremenesses mastery over nature. At the very end was Tai Shi Huihuang and his vanguard, Tai Shi Huihuang himself road on a chariot pulled by four albino elephants, attended to by servants fanning them and giving them water, while his vanguard rode on white horse mane chariots, bearing the finest of recurve bows.

Cheers of his supremenesss glory echoed for the three days the procession took to depart the capital, into the rural highways of his eternal realm which spans the plurality of the locality of the six directions. The great cobbled roads stretched even into the countryside of his imperial realm, they would make great pace, reaching a town each day to undertake supper, this march in friendly land would only last for around thirteen weeks, but across those thirteen weeks Tai Shi Huihuang was showered with praise and honour by all under his imperial banner. Food was stockpiled as they marched to ensure that even the lowliest of slaves serving in the army would not go hungry under the watch of Tai Shi Huihuang, for he is as magnanimous as he is land-hungry.

The opening march of the grand campaign along the Great Sea of the Emptied Bladder of Tai Shi Huihuang bore little fruit in terms of the pursuit of making his supremeness immortal, though of course, the Imperial Scholar of the Most Noble Sciences and Histories specifically regarding those relating to Immortality and the Locations where one might find it did not deceive his supremeness as indeed he marked many areas for immortality to be found. Despite the lack of immortality finding, Tai Shi Huihuang would conquer many smaller tribes and kingdoms who dared to exist outside his imperial jurisdiction. Chiefly among them were the kingdom of Kung, the kingdom of Gu and the tribe of Mu. 

The Kingdom of Kung fell following the decisive battles of Mung, Iung and Dung. The battle of Mung, named for the city of Mung nearby the battle ground, was an unsurprising crushing defeat for the forces of the Kingdom of Kung. Their puniness was shown threefold, first, the arrows of the Supreme Imperial Men-at-Arms rained upon them like the thunders of heaven. For thirty minutes the Mung defence forces had shade, and then they became shades. Screaming in agony as arrows overran their shields and turned them to mangled corpses. For three days birds would feast on the carrion made by the great hail of arrows. Tai Shi Huihuang would erect a statue made of their bones, picked clean by the birds which he would later have dipped in molten gold on his march back through this area following the battle of Iung. The battle of Iung would last around thirty seconds, as it involved Tai Shi Huihuang marching his army to their borders, the Iung garrison looking upon war elephants and surrendering with all haste. The battle of Dung was another unsurprising victory for Tai Shi Huihuang, it was named the battle of Dung as the enemy army soiled themselves before fleeing the field. 

Victory in the Kingdom of Kung was rapid, mere weeks before the fall of the King himself, and the adding of another tassel to Tai Shi Huihuangs mianguan-

Steps, rapid and deliberate steps towards where the young woman was supposed to be sleeping, she paused the drama on her phone, imported from Daesun. The model was sufficient for her needs - or so her mother said. Texting, calling, playing those dumb games and watching educational videos! Well this was educational, technically. Though of course she would not see it that way, it was just her staying up late on a school night again. Watching those damn S-Dramas. It's all communist propaganda, shed say that again when the door swung open.

And it did, and it was the exact same sing-song she had heard time and time again. Her mother stepped off the cold faux-wooden floor onto the soft carpet she had ordered of Memu with the little digitalised pocket money she got, when her mother didnt forget or her father didnt spend it all on drink. Her mother began her tirade. 

IT IS A SCHOOL NIGHT LITTLE MISSY, YOU NEED TO STOP WATCHING THAT DAMN COMMUNIST PROPAGANDA AND START FOCUSING ON YOUR SCHOOLING. YOU ARE NEARLY EIGHTEEN, YOU HEAR THAT? THE BIG EIGHT TEEN, YOUR ALMOST AN ADULT AND WHAT DO YOU HAVE TO SHOW FOR IT? BARELY PASSING WITH BS, ONE A IN ENGLISH. WHAT AM I SUPPOSED TO SAY TO MY FRIENDS? I HAVE TWO DISAPPOINTING CHILDREN AND A HUSBAND WHO LOVES A BOTTLE MORE THEN ME? START FOCUSING AND GET OFF THAT PHONE, WHY DID I EVEN LET YOU GET IT AFTER DOING NOTHING DURING YOUR SUMMER JOB 

She had stopped listening around this point, and started staring blankly at this woman who was supposed to be her mother. She thought of the Stuipendian Book Store by her school, one of few reasons she went to school anymore, that and the smokes that boys in her class sold. She started daydreaming of the bookstore while her mother continued to blather about how much her life sucked and therefore how much her daughter's life must suck in turn. 

In that bookstore there was peace, few entered in it, and those few who did were respectful of it and of her. Quiet tunes of the Erhu played, sometimes the kindly old man or his wife would play music she liked, or get somebody back home to record it on their Erhu and play it instrumentally, who would do that for her at home? Would her mother listen to things she found interest in, would her father? No, nothing, they didnt notice the yellow stains on her teeth, nor the smell of smoke in her hair. Only the collapsing grades because they were shoved in their faces. 

She was already sick of this conversation, if you can even call it that. She stopped caring about this place, or her government when she started noticing how little everyone cared when she did well. Started skipping when her parents only cared when she did poorly. Started going to that book shop with the kindly old elderly couple when her parents stopped acting like parents and more like roommates who despised her.

She learned from the kindly Mrs and Mr Xi. They doted on her, though they never seemed to go out, bar the grocery store. Even then she would start taking their money to do their shopping for them. It was odd, by then again, the whole International Proletarian Education Program was odd. But she didnt care. It was home, a true home. Her mind drifted off to some required reading they had to do in school. Of Mice and Men or something, well either way, she thought of the little home they dreamed of. If she was born in Stuipendia she could have had one of those homes, out in the north where Tai Shi Huihuang conquered. She could have lived the life of a farmer, toiling for a nation who loved her, and who she loved. Or a Peoples Historian, preserving the history of a land worthy to have their history kept alive.

Not like her home, not like New Westmore. Who killed the natives, who did nothing but say a handful of harsh words to Mizrahel after they committed genocide. She was tired of it all, but at least she had her respites. Smoking and the bookstore. Tomorrow she would go and smoke with the old Mr Xi, Mrs Xi didnt like it, the old man assured her every time. They smoked and talked about life, never drank. The old man hated it, and so did she. A father figure was found in that old man, and a motherly figure in his wife.

She was there for them, and them for her. Books piled up in her room, though with false covers to hide it from her Mother. Speaking of, where did she go? Mustve left at some point.

Whatever
 
The girl stopped caring a while ago, she would not go back to watching her drama, she would sleep. School, then the bookstore. Thats what shed do tomorrow.[/spoiler]
